decisions.choice: Quarantine every unaccepted Codex component, including hooks and agents
decisions.rationale: One trust rule must apply to every active runtime surface.

decisions.choice: Complete a global dependency census, then use complete vertical acceptance cycles
decisions.rationale: Expose hidden dependencies before each started component is carried through acceptance.

decisions.choice: Use one universal acceptance registry for all Codex component types
decisions.rationale: Skills, hooks, agents, settings, memory runtime, and orchestration need the same enforceable active-versus-accepted boundary.

decisions.choice: Hard-gate required dependencies before component acceptance
decisions.rationale: Prevent hidden degraded modes and plan port timing carefully to avoid current-use and dependency failures.

decisions.choice: Preserve prior partial-port work as untrusted historical evidence and independently reverify each claim before reuse
decisions.rationale: Keep potentially useful evidence without inheriting unreliable completion claims.

decisions.choice: Make deep-plan first and deep-research second after each one's required dependencies are accepted
decisions.rationale: Restore interactive decision planning first, then research, without bypassing their dependency chains.

decisions.choice: Commit and push after each accepted component; open one PR only after the complete port is accepted
decisions.rationale: Preserve recoverable progress without using a PR to signal incomplete work.

decisions.choice: Use one atomic transition after the universal gate and continuity map are ready
decisions.rationale: Avoid mismatches between active registrations and quarantined files.

decisions.choice: Use GitHub, Husky, AGENTS.md, Git status, and manual handoffs while nonessential Codex automation is paused
decisions.rationale: Avoid creating temporary unaccepted hooks.

decisions.choice: Govern every load-bearing Codex-port component, excluding ordinary planning records
decisions.rationale: Apply one enforceable acceptance meaning to all runtime and governance components.

decisions.choice: Classify dependencies as required, optional route, or evidence-only
decisions.rationale: Hard-gate true requirements while handling cyclic optional routes safely and explicitly.

decisions.choice: Universal gate, convergence-loop, then deep-plan
decisions.rationale: Restore deep-plan after its required verification dependency without waiting on optional routes.

decisions.choice: Accept all eight roles independently, then orchestration, then deep-research
decisions.rationale: Give every research dependency its own evidence, failure tests, approval, commit, and push.

decisions.choice: Superseded by decision 16
decisions.rationale: The earlier placement treated behavioral memory and dependency-bound memory machinery as one component; decision 16 corrects that model.

decisions.choice: Include brainstorm early in the accepted dependency sequence
decisions.rationale: Restore the operator's preferred ideation-to-research-to-planning workflow near the beginning of the rebuild.

decisions.choice: Complete and accept behavioral-memory reconciliation before the major workflow ports, then implement dependency-bound memory machinery at each earliest valid dependency point
decisions.rationale: Global operator rules and quality standards must govern the remaining port work from the start, while the memory section must remain incomplete until every required runtime mechanism is accepted and working.

decisions.choice: Require verified behavioral parity with an explicit source-to-target mapping
decisions.rationale: Preserve every source requirement and outcome while making Codex-native adaptations explicit, testable, and subject to operator approval.

decisions.choice: Reset every previous completion, active, deferred, and no-port conclusion to unverified historical evidence
decisions.rationale: Retain potentially useful prior work without allowing unreliable conclusions to define the new baseline.

decisions.choice: Use two-part acceptance and require both repository acceptance and operator installation verification for overall completion
decisions.rationale: Prevent repository-ready but uninstalled or untested machine behavior from being called complete.

decisions.choice: Track durable portable state and keep volatile, sensitive, cached, authentication, and machine-local state untracked
decisions.rationale: Preserve cross-machine decisions and recovery while avoiding sensitive data, repository noise, and machine-specific conflicts.

decisions.choice: Use an asset-and-behavior inventory nested under components
decisions.rationale: Account for every source file, behavior, destination, dependency, registration, state use, security boundary, test, and disposition instead of hiding omissions inside broad component buckets.

decisions.choice: Universal gate; atomic quarantine and restart verification; global census; behavioral memory; convergence-loop; deep-plan; contrarian-challenger; brainstorm; remaining research roles; research orchestration; deep-research, with dependency-bound memory machinery inserted at each earliest valid point
decisions.rationale: Establish trusted governance and global behavior first, preserve deep-plan priority, place brainstorm early, and satisfy every required dependency before activation.

decisions.choice: Only the operator's explicit approval may activate a component in the universal registry
decisions.rationale: Evidence establishes readiness but cannot authorize its own acceptance; the operator remains the sole reviewer and decision-maker.

decisions.choice: Require layered verification covering source mapping, static validation, positive fixtures, negative and failure paths, dependencies and registrations, real Codex runtime behavior, and operator approval
decisions.rationale: Prevent fixture-only or prose-only evidence from being mistaken for working runtime parity; any inapplicable category requires an operator-approved written reason.

decisions.choice: After the quarantine commit and push, restart Codex and verify a clean runtime before beginning any component port
decisions.rationale: Ensure definitions loaded before quarantine cannot contaminate discovery, testing, or acceptance of subsequent components.

decisions.choice: Require the operator's explicit approval for every exclusion, replacement, reduced scope, or deferral
decisions.rationale: Prevent implementation judgment from silently removing source requirements; each proposal must identify its evidence, consequences, alternatives, and recommendation.

decisions.choice: Stop the affected component, update the dependency graph, and obtain operator approval before resuming it
decisions.rationale: Keep scope and order changes visible while allowing only genuinely unaffected work to continue.

decisions.choice: Record source hashes, detect changes automatically, and invalidate affected mapping evidence until targeted re-review
decisions.rationale: Prevent accepted evidence from silently becoming stale when the preserved source implementation changes.

decisions.choice: Accept the smallest independently load-bearing component, grouping files only when separation would create a nonworking unit
decisions.rationale: Provide precise review and failure isolation for skills, agents, hooks, shared engines, registrations, memory layers, and runtime configuration.

decisions.choice: Discovery completes only when the entire port is mapped, every currently answerable gate is resolved, and the operator approves the complete plan inline
decisions.rationale: Prevent high-level ordering from being mistaken for a complete executable plan and prohibit unresolved scope from leaking into implementation.

decisions.choice: Complete every internal stub, dormant path, and deferred section of each included workflow, without automatically absorbing genuinely separate future products
decisions.rationale: Deliver complete included workflows while preventing references to unbuilt external systems from silently expanding the port into unrelated product development.

decisions.choice: Continue the repository's broader existing research and planning in a separate project after the Codex port is complete
decisions.rationale: Keep port completion bounded and verifiable while preserving a complete inventory and handoff of future-product research, plans, and unresolved roadmap work.

decisions.choice: Place the runtime-neutral schema and labeling subsystem under root-level sync/
decisions.rationale: Keep shared code, tests, schemas, and documentation together without misclassifying them as Claude- or Codex-specific runtime configuration.

decisions.choice: Include and complete the current labeling system in this port
decisions.rationale: The existing substantial Claude subsystem, label-audit workflow, and hook behavior are part of current parity even though broader cross-repository synchronization extensions belong to the later project.

decisions.choice: Require a real repository backfill, operator arbitration, catalog promotion, atomic hook activation, and live runtime verification
decisions.rationale: Prevent a tested library or dormant hook scaffold from being called a working labeling system and keep ambiguous labels under operator authority.

decisions.choice: Preserve .claude/ as the comparison source and create independently accepted shared and Codex targets with recorded source hashes
decisions.rationale: Maintain trustworthy source evidence and isolate Codex changes without coupling this port to a simultaneous Claude refactor.

decisions.choice: Preserve it as historical evidence, verify durable decisions are represented elsewhere, and do not activate it as Codex runtime state
decisions.rationale: Retain provenance without pretending stale Claude-specific execution state can safely resume in a different runtime.

decisions.choice: Use layered enforcement across Codex hooks, shared deterministic checks, Husky, GitHub protections, and universal acceptance-registry validation
decisions.rationale: Codex hooks provide immediate feedback but are not a complete enforcement boundary; shared logic and independent repository controls prevent one disabled or bypassed surface from removing protection.

decisions.choice: Use a layered context-safety replacement and explicitly accept the documented Codex specialized-tool interception boundary
decisions.rationale: Preserve size-first and bounded-reading behavior across observable shell, MCP, and local tool paths without falsely claiming universal interception that Codex does not expose.

decisions.choice: Notify directly from the producing failure path using durable pending state, immediate system context, repeated acknowledgment warnings, best-available terminal notification, and operator-verified user-level delivery where applicable
decisions.rationale: Replace the unavailable Claude Notification hook event with redundant delivery tied directly to the failure, while respecting project-versus-user configuration boundaries.

decisions.choice: Use an explicit complete session-end skill as the primary interactive workflow and a bounded SessionEnd hook only for emergency preservation
decisions.rationale: Codex SessionEnd timing and its three-second limit cannot perform the source workflow's interactive review, decisions, commit, and push sequence.

decisions.choice: Do not port the Claude status-line capability or build a Codex replacement
decisions.rationale: The operator explicitly approved statusline as a final port exclusion; preserve the Claude source as historical evidence without assigning replacement work to this or the later continuation project.

decisions.choice: Complete and verify the real route-specific Context7, Memory MCP, and SonarCloud integrations; treat unused permission-only MCP entries as evidence-only
decisions.rationale: Preserve actual workflow capabilities without turning unrelated MCP services into global dependencies or allowing unavailable optional routes to degrade silently.

decisions.choice: Expand the Codex deep-plan workflow to support multi-phase projects, milestones, phase decomposition, dependency ordering, durable project state, and execution handoff
decisions.rationale: Replace unavailable external GSD commands with a complete self-contained Codex planning outcome instead of retaining broken routes.

decisions.choice: Build a complete bounded structured debt-intake system with guarded mutations, generated review output, lifecycle operations, cross-links, and layered tests
decisions.rationale: Deep-research, PR review, and pre-commit repair require a real debt workflow rather than the current Markdown append stub; broader analytics remain subject to separate decisions.

decisions.choice: Partially resolved: build complete create-audit, skill-ecosystem-audit, hook-ecosystem-audit, PR-retro, and systematic-debugging capabilities; implement quick-fix as a bounded explicit mode of pre-commit-fixer. Remaining named routes still require individual decisions.
decisions.rationale: The operator approved Q46.1 through Q46.6. These are real workflow requirements, not handoff buckets: the three audits retain their distinct scopes, PR-retro closes the existing learning loop, systematic-debugging remains reusable, and quick-fix shares the pre-commit repair engine without duplicating it. No unreviewed route is implicitly deferred or included.

subdecisions.choice: Build a complete separate create-audit workflow.
Build a complete orchestrated skill-ecosystem audit with eight dimensions, shared rules, synthesis, review, and remediation.
Build a complete hook-ecosystem audit workflow.
Build a standalone complete PR retrospective that consumes PR learnings and proposes memory or workflow promotion through operator approval.
Build a complete reusable systematic-debugging workflow.
Implement quick-fix as a bounded explicit mode of pre-commit-fixer rather than as a separate skill.

decisions.choice: Separate configuration and authentication health from live tool-capability preflight
decisions.rationale: Do not report configured server names as availability; workflows must verify a real tool route before relying on it without exposing secrets.

decisions.choice: Require a complete gap-inventory analysis comparison before plan approval and repeat it before final port completion
decisions.rationale: Prove that every source asset, behavior, dependency, route, state contract, registration, test, prior conclusion, approved exclusion, platform replacement, and separate-project boundary is accounted for in the plan and then in accepted working implementation.
